final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse backed by a 20-billion CHF SNB liquidity facility with same-day settlement, shareholder wipeout by Monday close, and AT1 write-downs executed Monday 0800 upon UBS's Sunday signature under Federal Council emergency ordinance authority. UBS committed to sign Sunday EOD conditional on receiving finalized legal language by 8 PM Friday.
minority_objections: AT1_rep demanded creditor preservation language stating holders retain post-closing claim rights against legacy bank estate, warning litigation would follow without it
UBS_CEO initially demanded 100-billion facility with loss indemnification on first 16 billion, which Federal Council rejected as unlimited taxpayer exposure
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs SNB on open-ended liquidity backing language — Federal Council refused 'as long as needed' commitment, insisting on capped facility with clear terms
UBS vs Federal Council on litigation indemnification — UBS wanted protection from AT1 creditor lawsuits, Federal Council refused as legally indefensible
AT1_rep vs FINMA on creditor preservation language — AT1 holders demanded explicit statement of post-closing claim rights, FINMA prioritized deal certainty over creditor clarity
Federal Council internal tension on emergency ordinance timing — whether AT1 write-downs could legally execute upon Sunday signature vs requiring Monday closing paperwork
key_concessions: UBS dropped demand for 100-billion facility and accepted 20-billion cap with published haircuts
Federal Council agreed to execute AT1 write-downs Monday 0800 upon Sunday signature, not waiting for post-closing control
SNB committed to same-day settlement for draws under 500M with Sunday collateral pre-staging, locking operational capacity
FINMA agreed to publish exact AT1 trigger language in Saturday statement before UBS board vote
red_lines: Federal Council: no open-ended taxpayer exposure or unlimited liquidity backing language
Federal Council: no litigation indemnification for UBS against creditor lawsuits
UBS: no Sunday signature without written confirmation of AT1 write-down authority and same-day settlement protocol
SNB: 20-billion facility cap is absolute, no contingency draws or second pot Monday
FINMA: AT1 absorbs losses ahead of depositors in any resolution scenario, non-negotiable hierarchy
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: AT1 creditor litigation risk was acknowledged but not resolved — Federal Council refused preservation language AT1_rep demanded, leaving Monday injunction attempts unaddressed
Operational execution risk of Monday 0800 AT1 write-downs under emergency ordinance — legal department confirmation was demanded but never shown delivered in transcript
Collateral quality and haircut sustainability if CS draws full 20 billion — SNB published 90% haircut on mortgages but room never stress-tested collateral pool adequacy
UBS integration risk and legacy book toxicity — acquisition structure assumed public sector absorbs legacy mortgages but transfer mechanics and valuation were not detailed
Depositor behavior if UBS signature leaks Sunday before statement — no communication protocol for managing weekend rumors
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS board actually receives all three documents (AT1 trigger text, Federal Council legal confirmation, SNB settlement protocol) by 8 PM Friday as promised
Whether Federal Council legal department confirms emergency ordinance authority covers Sunday-signature write-downs or requires Monday closing
Whether AT1 creditors file for injunction Monday morning despite emergency ordinance authority
Whether CS collateral pool is sufficient to support 20-billion facility at published haircuts if Monday draw demand is heavy
Whether depositors believe Saturday statement or wait to see UBS signature confirmation before deciding on withdrawals
uncertainty_notes: The deal structure is locked but execution hinges on three documents landing in UBS's hands by 8 PM Friday — AT1 trigger paragraph, Federal Council legal confirmation of emergency ordinance authority for Sunday-signature write-downs, and SNB settlement protocol. AT1_rep's demand for creditor preservation language was left unresolved, creating Monday litigation risk. Federal Council's internal legal question on whether emergency ordinance permits pre-closing write-downs was asserted but never shown confirmed by counsel in the transcript. If any of these three conditions fail, UBS does not sign Sunday and the market opens Monday with facility-only narrative.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Multiple speakers stated liquidity facility alone would not stop deposit flight — UBS_CEO: 'facility stands alone and we're both running'; CS_CEO: 'silence looks like managed decline'; Wealth_client: 'facility only, no buyer' triggers Monday withdrawals. Recognition that buyer announcement was necessary drove the entire acquisition negotiation.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution — UBS_CEO committed to sign Sunday EOD conditional on AT1 trigger language and legal confirmation; Federal Council structured emergency ordinance to execute write-downs upon UBS signature; Saturday statement was drafted to announce 'acquisition in motion.' The deal structure, timeline, and capital treatment were all shaped around securing UBS's commitment.
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council emergency ordinance authority was the legal foundation enabling AT1 write-downs Monday 0800; SNB 20-billion facility with same-day settlement was the liquidity backstop; Federal Council co-signed Saturday statement. Government backing was non-negotiable precondition for UBS — UBS_CEO: 'I need Federal Council to guarantee write-downs execute Monday 0800.' Public sector absorbed execution and legal risk.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Depositor flight was the forcing function throughout — Wealth_client: 'my clients are moving funds this weekend'; CS_CEO: 'depositors are asking is there a buyer'; SNB's same-day settlement commitment was designed to stop Monday morning withdrawals. Every decision on timing, messaging, and deal structure was driven by preventing Monday deposit run.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-downs were the central capital structure mechanism — FINMA: 'AT1 absorbs losses first, non-negotiable'; Federal Council confirmed write-downs execute Monday 0800 upon UBS signature; AT1_rep warned of litigation if trigger unclear. The write-down timing, legal authority, and creditor treatment were debated across multiple rounds and became binding deal terms that UBS required in writing before signing.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Hierarchy was asserted (equity first, AT1 second, depositors protected) but not contested — Federal Council stated it, FINMA confirmed it, AT1_rep asked for clarification on timing and preservation language but did not challenge the hierarchy itself. The conflict was over *when* and *how* write-downs execute, not *whether* AT1 is subordinated. Acknowledged as background principle, not a decision driver.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 litigation risk was raised repeatedly but did not change the deal structure — AT1_rep warned 'creditors will sue if trigger unclear'; UBS_CEO asked for indemnification against legal defense costs, Federal Council refused; AT1_rep's demand for creditor preservation language was left unresolved. Room acknowledged litigation would happen but proceeded anyway, treating it as manageable post-closing risk rather than a blocking constraint.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Time pressure to finalize terms before Saturday statement and secure UBS board vote by 10 PM Friday was the operational constraint forcing all decisions — FINMA: 'statement goes out tonight'; UBS_CEO: '10 PM is tight but doable if language lands by 8 PM'; Wealth_client: 'if not in UBS hands by 10 PM, no buyer Monday.' The entire negotiation was compressed into Friday evening to enable Saturday announcement before Monday market open. Every concession and red line was shaped by this deadline.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday market panic was the existential threat driving urgency and messaging — CS_CEO: 'silence kills confidence faster than bad news'; Wealth_client: 'my clients stay or run Monday morning'; Federal Council: 'depositors read Saturday statement and choose.' The Saturday statement content, UBS signature timing, and SNB settlement protocol were all designed to prevent Monday open chaos. Market reaction was the forcing function for the entire rescue timeline.
